Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))$. For the given values, $\ln1000/\ln(20/19)\approx134.7$ (with $\ln1000\approx6.9078$ and $\ln(20/19)\approx0.051293$), so $N=135$. Under the convex scenario-program assumptions, at most one sample can support the one-variable solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.
            (b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.
            (c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)\approx5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)\approx115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}\approx0.911$. Hoeffding supplies the lower confidence bound $1-e^{-0.0928}\approx9\%$, rather than $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).
            (d) For a fixed $K^\ast$ and one fresh independent batch of at least $5757$ validation samples from the normalized $c=0.95$ credible posterior, with probability at least $0.99$ over that batch, acceptance (empirical stability at least $0.95$) implies that the full posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $0.95-0.05-0.02=0.88$: a Bayesian statement, as good as the GP posterior. This is a fixed-batch implication; repeated validation attempts need a separate failure budget.

full_linked_scenario_and_validation_cont:
Definition — Hoeffding's inequality and sub-Gaussianity
For i.i.d. $Z_1,\dots,Z_p\in[a,b]$ with mean $\mu$ and $\bar Z=\frac1p\sum_iZ_i$: $\ \mathbb P[\bar Z-\mu\ge t]\le\exp\big(-2pt^2/(b-a)^2\big)$, and twice that for $|\bar Z-\mu|$. For indicators, $\mu\ge\bar Z-t$ at confidence $1-\delta$ needs $p\ge\ln(1/\delta)/(2t^2)$. The proof rests on Hoeffding's lemma: a variable in $[a,b]$ is $\tfrac{b-a}2$-sub-Gaussian, the noise model of the GP bounds in Module 3. Use: a-posteriori validation of a fixed design.
Theorem — The scenario approach (Calafiore & Campi 2006; exact bound of Campi & Garatti 2008)
Setting. A convex program with $d$ decision variables and uncertain convex constraints $\theta\in\Theta_\delta$, $\delta\sim P$ (in this box $\delta$ is the uncertain parameter, as in the scenario literature, not a failure probability; $\theta$ is the decision variable, not a policy parameter). Solve the scenario program $\min c^\top\theta$ s.t. $\theta\in\Theta_{\delta^{(i)}}$ for $N$ i.i.d. samples; the required finite instances, including singleton problems, constraint removals and one-constraint augmentations, are assumed feasible with nonempty feasible interiors and attained unique minimisers of the original linear objective; the optimiser and violation event are measurable. Merely selecting one point from a nonunique optimum set does not supply these assumptions: a tie-break variant needs its own support/compression argument before using the same dimension-$d$ bound. Violation probability: $V(\theta)=P\{\delta:\theta\notin\Theta_\delta\}$.
Statement. For any $P$ (binomial tails: Primer C), $$P^N\big\{V(\theta_N^\ast)\gt\epsilon\big\}\ \le\ \sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\binom Ni\epsilon^i(1-\epsilon)^{N-i},$$ with equality for fully-supported problems (Campi & Garatti, SIAM J. Optim. 2008), sharpening the earlier $\binom Nd(1-\epsilon)^{N-d}$ (Calafiore & Campi, TAC 2006, their eq. 11, from which their explicit sample-size formulas are derived). A simple sufficient size, which follows from a Chernoff bound on the binomial tail and is the form von Rohr et al. use (after Campi, Garatti & Prandini, Annu. Rev. Control 2009), is $N\ge\frac2\epsilon(\ln\frac1\beta+d)$.
In words. At most $d$ sampled constraints support the solution, so violating more than an $\epsilon$-fraction has binomial-tail probability. Use: a-priori design of convex (e.g. LMI) controllers. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$, $d=10$: exact $N=581$, older bound 1344, sufficient formula 861 (our computation).
Reading the statement. A support constraint is a sampled constraint whose removal changes the solution; convexity together with those original-objective uniqueness assumptions allows at most $d$ of them; arbitrary selection from a nonunique optimum set need not preserve this count. Fully supported means that, with probability one, the solution has exactly $d$ of them; only the equality case needs this. There are two probability levels: $V(\theta)$ is the probability that one fresh uncertain system violates the design, while $P^N\{V(\theta_N^\ast)\gt\epsilon\}$ is the probability, over the $N$ design samples, of drawing a sample that produces a design with $V\gt\epsilon$. The sample-size calculator below applies only to feasible convex scenario programs with the solution assumptions above.

von Rohr, Neumann-Brosig & Trimpe, L4DC 2021 differentiate a GP dynamics model at the operating point, obtaining a Bayesian (matrix-normal) posterior over $S=[\bar A\ \bar B]$, truncated to its credible region of mass $c$ (a region of posterior probability $c$; Primer C). With $\phi_K=\mathbb 1[\rho(\bar A+\bar BK)\lt1]$ they seek $\mathbb E[\phi_K]\ge1-\epsilon$ at minimal expected LQR cost. A priori: the initial controller solves a common-Lyapunov LMI over $M$ sampled systems, a convex scenario program with $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables; their Theorem 1 gives $\mathbb E[\phi_{K_{\mathrm{init}}}]\ge1-\epsilon$ with probability greater than $1-\beta$ if $M\ge\lceil\frac2\epsilon(\ln\frac1\beta+n_k)\rceil$. A posteriori: the improvement steps (a majorise–minimise scheme averaging over samples; see the MM background in Section 3) are not a scenario program, so the final $K^\ast$ is returned only if its empirical stability rate on $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ fresh samples satisfies $\hat\phi\ge1-\epsilon$.

Background — Derivatives of a GP, matrix-normal posteriors and the common-Lyapunov LMI

Derivatives of a GP. If the mean $m_a$ and covariance $k_{ab}(z,z')$ of a vector-valued GP have continuous mixed second derivatives near the operating point, difference quotients are linear combinations of jointly Gaussian values, and their mean-square limits, the partial derivatives, are again jointly Gaussian with mean $\partial_im_a(z)$ and covariance

$$\operatorname{Cov}\big(\partial_if_a(z),\partial_jf_b(z')\big)=\partial_{z_i}\partial_{z'_j}k_{ab}(z,z').$$

Conditioning on data with Gaussian noise (Primer C) gives a Gaussian posterior over these derivatives, i.e. over the entries of $S=[\bar A\ \bar B]$. Matrix-normal is a special, separable structure: $\operatorname{vec}(S)\sim\mathcal N(\operatorname{vec}(M),C\otimes R)$, with $R$ the covariance between rows, $C$ between columns, and $C\otimes R$ the block matrix with blocks $C_{ij}R$; general derivative posteriors need not have it. Either way this is uncertainty about a local linearisation, not a nonlinear stability certificate.

The common-Lyapunov LMI. For sampled systems $(A_i,B_i)$ look for $X\succ0$ and $Y$ with

$$\begin{bmatrix}X&(A_iX+B_iY)^\top\\A_iX+B_iY&X\end{bmatrix}\succ0\quad\text{for every }i,\qquad K:=YX^{-1}.$$

With $Y=KX$ the off-diagonal block is $(A_i+B_iK)X$; the Schur complement (Module 2) turns the LMI into $X-X(A_i+B_iK)^\top X^{-1}(A_i+B_iK)X\succ0$, and multiplying by $X^{-1}$ on both sides gives $(A_i+B_iK)^\top P(A_i+B_iK)-P\prec0$ with $P=X^{-1}$: one Lyapunov matrix for all sampled systems. The conditions are linear in $(X,Y)$, so this is a convex scenario program; its $n_k$ must count all scalar decision variables, including any performance variables.

Caveat — corrected statement of the validation theorem (von Rohr et al. 2021, Theorem 2)
Theorem 2 prints $M_{\mathrm{val}}\ge\frac1{2\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}}\log\frac1\alpha$, but its proof uses $\mathbb P(\hat\phi-\mathbb E\phi\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}})\le e^{-2M_{\mathrm{val}}\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}^2}$, which is at most $\alpha$ only if $$M_{\mathrm{val}}\ \ge\ \frac{\log(1/\alpha)}{2\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}^2}:$$ for $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, 5757 samples instead of the printed 116. Eq. (8) prints $\mathbb P(\mathbb E[\phi_{K^\ast}]\ge1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{pr}})\gt1-\alpha$ with $\epsilon_{\mathrm{pr}}=c-(\epsilon+\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}})$, whereas the proof concludes $\mathbb P(\mathbb E[\phi]\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{pr}})\le\alpha$. Consistent statement: with probability at least $1-\alpha$ over the validation samples, the posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $c-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$, since Hoeffding gives $\mathbb E_{P_c}[\phi]\ge1-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$ on the truncated posterior and truncation removes mass $1-c$: $\mathbb E_P[\phi]\ge c(1-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}})\ge c-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$. Both slips are visible in the full text (statement versus proof); arXiv v2 fixes a different typo in Algorithm 1. This guarantee is Bayesian, unlike Fiedler et al.'s, and the algorithm repeats until the test passes, so the union-bound remark of Section 6 applies.

Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))$. For the given values, $\ln1000/\ln(20/19)\approx134.7$ (with $\ln1000\approx6.9078$ and $\ln(20/19)\approx0.051293$), so $N=135$. Under the convex scenario-program assumptions, at most one sample can support the one-variable solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.

  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := actual_sample_maximum_is_attained_by_a_sample s
  have hki : k = i := by

  have he : sampleMaximum s = s i := hki ▸ hk

  intro j hj

    · intro j hj

    · rw [hm]
      linarith

    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum)
    (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (hi : supportsAt domain constraints optimum i)
    (hj : supportsAt domain constraints optimum j) : False := by
  obtain ⟨x, hxd, hx, hxo⟩ := hi
  obtain ⟨y, hyd, hy, hyo⟩ := hj
  rcases le_total x y with hxy | hyx
  · have hcy : y ∈ constraints j :=

      refine ⟨hyd, ?_⟩

      · exact hy k hkj
    exact (not_le_of_gt hyo) (hopt.2 hf)
  · have hcx : x ∈ constraints i :=
      (hc i).ordConnected.out (hy i hij) (hopt.1.2 i) ⟨hyx, hxo.le⟩
    have hf : x ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hxd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hki : k = i
      · exact hki ▸ hcx
      · exact hx k hki
    exact (not_le_of_gt hxo) (hopt.2 hf)

  intro i hi j hj

    (hOne : ∀t,IsLeast (domain∩C t) (one t))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (s : Fin n→Θ) :
    IsLeast (actualSampledFeasible domain C n s)
      (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))) := by
  classical
  let m := sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))
  obtain ⟨z,hzd,hzs,_⟩ := hJoint s (s 0)
  have hmz : m≤z := by
    exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty _).mpr
      (fun i _ => (hOne (s i)).2 ⟨hzd,hzs i⟩)
  have hlow : ∀i,one (s i)≤ m := by
    intro i
    change one (s i) ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun j=>one (s j))
    exact Finset.le_sup' (fun j=>one (s j)) (Finset.mem_univ i)
  obtain ⟨i,_,hi⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun i=>one (s i))
  have him : m=one (s i) := hi
  refine ⟨⟨?_,?_⟩,?_⟩
  · change m ∈ domain
    rw [him];exact (hOne (s i)).1.1
  · intro j
    exact (hconv (s j)).ordConnected.out (hOne (s j)).1.2 (hzs j) ⟨hlow j,hmz⟩
  · intro x hx
    exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty _).mpr
      (fun j _=>(hOne (s j)).2 ⟨hx.1,hx.2 j⟩)

/-- Actual fresh-constraint violation is a strict lower-optimizer tail, even when
individual convex constraints have both an upper and a lower boundary. -/
theorem actual_general_interval_fresh_violation_iff_single_optimizer_above
    {Θ : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ)
    (hconv : ∀t,Convex ℝ (C t))
    (hOne : ∀t,IsLeast (domain∩C t) (one t))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (s : Fin n→Θ) (t : Θ) :
    sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))∉C t ↔
      sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))<one t := by
  let m := sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))
  have hopt := actual_general_interval_program_optimizer_is_the_maximum_single_optimizer
    domain C one hconv hOne n hJoint s
  have hmd : m∈domain := hopt.1.1
  constructor
  · intro hnot
    by_contra hn
    have hlo : one t≤ m := le_of_not_gt hn
    obtain ⟨z,hzd,hzs,hzt⟩ := hJoint s t
    have hmz : m≤z := hopt.2 ⟨hzd,hzs⟩
    exact hnot ((hconv t).ordConnected.out (hOne t).1.2 hzt ⟨hlo,hmz⟩)
  · intro hlt hmem
    exact (not_le_of_gt hlt) ((hOne t).2 ⟨hmd,hmem⟩)

/-- The actual optimized convex program's risk is derived from its generated
single-constraint optimizer law, without a postulated risk distribution. -/
theorem actual_interval_optimized_risk_equals_the_cdf_tail
    {Θ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] (law : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (domain : Set ℝ) (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ) (hMeas : Measurable one)
    (hconv : ∀t,Convex ℝ (C t))
    (hOne : ∀t,IsLeast (domain∩C t) (one t))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (s : Fin n→Θ) :
    actualViolation law C (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i)))=
      1-cdf (law.map one) (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))) := by
  haveI : IsProbabilityMeasure (law.map one) := (Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map_iff hMeas.aemeasurable).mpr inferInstance
  have he : {t | sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))∉C t}=
      one ⁻¹' Ioi (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))) := by
    ext t
    exact actual_general_interval_fresh_violation_iff_single_optimizer_above
      domain C one hconv hOne n hJoint s t
  rw [actualViolation,he]
  have hmap := Measure.map_apply (μ:=law) hMeas (measurableSet_Ioi (a:=sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))))
  change (law (one ⁻¹' Ioi (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (s i))))).toReal=_
  rw [←hmap]
  exact actual_fresh_constraint_violation_is_one_minus_its_cdf (law.map one) _

/-- The one-dimensional optimized scenario-risk bound for arbitrary common laws.
Atoms only improve the inequality; continuity is not assumed. -/
theorem actual_iid_general_convex_interval_optimizer_risk_bound
    {Θ Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (law : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (domain : Set ℝ) (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ) (hMeas : Measurable one)
    (hconv : ∀t,Convex ℝ (C t))
    (hOne : ∀t,IsLeast (domain∩C t) (one t))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (X : Fin n→Ω→Θ) (hm : ∀i,Measurable (X i))
    (hind : iIndepFun X P) (hlaw : ∀i,HasLaw (X i) law P)
    (epsilon : ℝ) (he : epsilon∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    P.real {w | epsilon<actualViolation law C
      (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (X i w)))} ≤ (1-epsilon)^n := by
  haveI : IsProbabilityMeasure (law.map one) := (Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map_iff hMeas.aemeasurable).mpr inferInstance
  let Y : Fin n→Ω→ℝ := fun i w=>one (X i w)
  have hY : iIndepFun Y P := hind.comp (fun _=>one) (fun _=>hMeas)
  have hYL : ∀i,HasLaw (Y i) (law.map one) P := by
    intro i
    exact (show HasLaw one (law.map one) law from ⟨hMeas.aemeasurable,rfl⟩).comp (hlaw i)
  have hcdf : Measurable (cdf (law.map one)) := (monotone_cdf (law.map one)).measurable
  let Z : Fin n→Ω→ℝ := fun i w=>cdf (law.map one) (Y i w)
  have hZ : iIndepFun Z P := hY.comp (fun _=>cdf (law.map one)) (fun _=>hcdf)
  have hp : ∀i,P.real {w | Z i w<1-epsilon} ≤ 1-epsilon := by
    intro i
    have hl := ((show HasLaw (cdf (law.map one))
        ((law.map one).map (cdf (law.map one))) (law.map one) from
        ⟨hcdf.aemeasurable,rfl⟩).comp (hYL i)).measureReal_eq (measurableSet_Iio (a:=1-epsilon))
    change P.real {w | Z i w<1-epsilon}=
      ((law.map one).map (cdf (law.map one))).real (Iio (1-epsilon)) at hl
    rw [hl]
    have hmap := Measure.map_apply (μ:=law.map one) hcdf (measurableSet_Iio (a:=1-epsilon))
    change (((law.map one).map (cdf (law.map one))) (Iio (1-epsilon))).toReal≤_
    rw [hmap]
    exact actual_arbitrary_cdf_strict_lower_probability_bound (law.map one)
      (1-epsilon) (by linarith [he.2])
  have hevent : {w | epsilon<actualViolation law C
      (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (X i w)))}=⋂i,{w | Z i w<1-epsilon} := by
    have heq : {w | epsilon<actualViolation law C
        (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (X i w)))}=
        {w | epsilon<violation (law.map one) (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>Y i w))} := by
      ext w
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      rw [actual_interval_optimized_risk_equals_the_cdf_tail law domain C one hMeas
        hconv hOne n hJoint (fun i=>X i w),
        actual_fresh_constraint_violation_is_one_minus_its_cdf]
    rw [heq,actual_optimized_violation_event_is_all_cdf_coordinates_below_threshold]
  have hprod := hZ.meas_iInter (s:=fun i=>{w | Z i w<1-epsilon})
    (fun i=>measurableSet_Iio.preimage (comap_measurable (Z i)))
  have hr := congrArg ENNReal.toReal hprod
  simp only [ENNReal.toReal_prod] at hr
  change P.real (⋂i,{w | Z i w<1-epsilon})=∏i,P.real {w | Z i w<1-epsilon} at hr
  rw [hevent,hr]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∏_i : Fin n,(1-epsilon) := Finset.prod_le_prod₀
      (fun i _=>measureReal_nonneg) (fun i _=>hp i)
    _ = (1-epsilon)^n := by simp

end SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovConvexIntervalRisk26

def orientedSet (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) : Set ℝ := {y | y/a∈S}

/-- An invertible scalar objective transforms actual convex constraints to convex intervals. -/
theorem actual_linear_objective_constraint_orientation_preserves_convexity
    (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (hS : Convex ℝ S) : Convex ℝ (orientedSet a S) := by
  have hx := hS.linear_preimage (a⁻¹ • (LinearMap.id : ℝ→ₗ[ℝ]ℝ))
  change Convex ℝ {y | a⁻¹*y∈S} at hx
  simpa only [orientedSet,div_eq_mul_inv,mul_comm] using hx

/-- An actual attained singleton linear-cost minimizer becomes an actual least scalar coordinate. -/
theorem actual_linear_objective_singleton_minimizer_becomes_least
    (a : ℝ) (ha : a≠0) (domain S : Set ℝ) (one : ℝ)
    (hmem : one∈domain∩S)
    (hmin : ∀x∈domain∩S,a*one≤a*x) :
    IsLeast (orientedSet a domain∩orientedSet a S) (a*one) := by
  constructor
  · simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hmem
  · intro y hy
    have h := hmin (y/a) ⟨hy.1,hy.2⟩
    have he : a*(y/a)=y := by field_simp [ha]
    simpa only [he] using h

/-- The actual optimizer of any nonzero scalar linear objective, with either sign,
    inherits the derived optimized scenario-risk law. -/
theorem actual_iid_nonzero_scalar_linear_convex_program_risk_bound
    {Θ Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (law : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (a : ℝ) (ha : a≠0) (domain : Set ℝ) (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ)
    (hmeas : Measurable one) (hconv : ∀t,Convex ℝ (C t))
    (hmem : ∀t,one t∈domain∩C t)
    (hmin : ∀t,∀x∈domain∩C t,a*one t≤a*x)
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (X : Fin n→Ω→Θ) (hm : ∀i,Measurable (X i))
    (hind : iIndepFun X P) (hlaw : ∀i,HasLaw (X i) law P)
    (epsilon : ℝ) (he : epsilon∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    P.real {w | epsilon<actualViolation law C
      (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>a*one (X i w))/a)} ≤ (1-epsilon)^n := by
  have ho : ∀t,IsLeast (orientedSet a domain∩orientedSet a (C t)) (a*one t) :=
    fun t=>actual_linear_objective_singleton_minimizer_becomes_least a ha domain
      (C t) (one t) (hmem t) (hmin t)
  have hj : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃y∈orientedSet a domain,
      (∀i,y∈orientedSet a (C (s i)))∧y∈orientedSet a (C t) := by
    intro s t
    obtain ⟨x,hxd,hxs,hxt⟩:=hJoint s t
    exact ⟨a*x,by simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hxd,
      fun i=>by simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hxs i,
      by simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hxt⟩
  have hc : ∀t,Convex ℝ (orientedSet a (C t)) :=
    fun t=>actual_linear_objective_constraint_orientation_preserves_convexity a (C t) (hconv t)
  have hr:=actual_iid_general_convex_interval_optimizer_risk_bound law P
    (orientedSet a domain) (fun t=>orientedSet a (C t)) (fun t=>a*one t)
    (measurable_const.mul hmeas) hc ho n hj X hm hind hlaw epsilon he
  simpa only [actualViolation,orientedSet,Set.mem_setOf_eq] using hr

/-- The normalized coordinate is genuinely a feasible global linear-cost optimizer. -/
theorem actual_scalar_linear_program_optimizer_feasible_and_global
    {Θ : Type*} (a : ℝ) (ha : a≠0) (domain : Set ℝ)
    (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ) (hconv : ∀t,Convex ℝ (C t))
    (hmem : ∀t,one t∈domain∩C t)
    (hmin : ∀t,∀x∈domain∩C t,a*one t≤a*x)
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (s : Fin n→Θ) :
    let opt := sampleMaximum n (fun i=>a*one (s i))/a
    opt∈actualSampledFeasible domain C n s ∧
      ∀x∈actualSampledFeasible domain C n s,a*opt≤a*x := by
  have ho : ∀t,IsLeast (orientedSet a domain∩orientedSet a (C t)) (a*one t) :=
    fun t=>actual_linear_objective_singleton_minimizer_becomes_least a ha domain
      (C t) (one t) (hmem t) (hmin t)
  have hj : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃y∈orientedSet a domain,
      (∀i,y∈orientedSet a (C (s i)))∧y∈orientedSet a (C t) := by
    intro s t
    obtain ⟨x,hxd,hxs,hxt⟩:=hJoint s t
    exact ⟨a*x,by simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hxd,
      fun i=>by simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hxs i,
      by simpa [orientedSet,ha] using hxt⟩
  have hp:=actual_general_interval_program_optimizer_is_the_maximum_single_optimizer
    (orientedSet a domain) (fun t=>orientedSet a (C t)) (fun t=>a*one t)
    (fun t=>actual_linear_objective_constraint_orientation_preserves_convexity a (C t) (hconv t))
    ho n hj s
  refine ⟨hp.1,?_⟩
  intro x hx
  have hmx : a*x∈actualSampledFeasible (orientedSet a domain)
      (fun t=>orientedSet a (C t)) n s := by
    change (a*x)/a∈domain ∧ ∀i,(a*x)/a∈C (s i)
    simpa [ha,actualSampledFeasible] using hx
  have h:=hp.2 hmx
  have he : a*(sampleMaximum n (fun i=>a*one (s i))/a)=
      sampleMaximum n (fun i=>a*one (s i)) := by field_simp [ha]
  rw [he]
  exact h

/-- A zero linear objective with the scenario uniqueness hypothesis has no fresh risk:
    uniqueness forces every jointly feasible value to equal the singleton optimizer. -/
theorem actual_zero_objective_unique_program_has_zero_fresh_risk
    {Θ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] (law : Measure Θ)
    (domain : Set ℝ) (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ)
    (hunique : ∀t,∀x∈domain∩C t,x=one t)
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hJoint : ∀(s : Fin n→Θ)(t : Θ),∃x∈domain,(∀i,x∈C (s i))∧x∈C t)
    (s : Fin n→Θ) : actualViolation law C (one (s 0))=0 := by
  have hgood : ∀t,one (s 0)∈C t := by
    intro t
    obtain ⟨x,hxd,hxs,hxt⟩:=hJoint s t
    have hx:=hunique (s 0) x ⟨hxd,hxs 0⟩
    simpa [←hx] using hxt
  have hempty : {t | one (s 0)∉C t}=(∅ : Set Θ) := by
    ext t
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq,Set.mem_empty_iff_false,iff_false]
    exact not_not_intro (hgood t)
  simp [actualViolation,hempty]


/-- The fixed common-law CDF upper region has at least epsilon mass, including atoms. -/
theorem actual_single_optimizer_upper_region_has_mass_at_least_epsilon
    {Θ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] (law : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (one : Θ→ℝ) (hmeas : Measurable one) (epsilon : ℝ) (he : epsilon≤1) :
    epsilon≤law.real {t | 1-epsilon≤cdf (law.map one) (one t)} := by
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (law.map one) :=
    (Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map_iff hmeas.aemeasurable).mpr inferInstance
  have hc : Measurable (cdf (law.map one)) := (monotone_cdf (law.map one)).measurable
  have hset : MeasurableSet {x : ℝ | cdf (law.map one) x<1-epsilon} :=
    measurableSet_lt hc measurable_const
  have hm:=Measure.map_apply (μ:=law) hmeas hset
  have hp:=actual_arbitrary_cdf_strict_lower_probability_bound (law.map one)
    (1-epsilon) (by linarith)
  have hA : MeasurableSet {t | cdf (law.map one) (one t)<1-epsilon} :=
    hset.preimage hmeas
  have hr : law.real {t | cdf (law.map one) (one t)<1-epsilon}≤1-epsilon := by
    change (law (one ⁻¹' {x : ℝ | cdf (law.map one) x<1-epsilon})).toReal≤_
    rw [←hm]
    exact hp
  have heq : {t | 1-epsilon≤cdf (law.map one) (one t)}=
      {t | cdf (law.map one) (one t)<1-epsilon}ᶜ := by
    ext t
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq,Set.mem_compl_iff,not_lt]
  rw [heq,probReal_compl_eq_one_sub hA]
  linarith

/-- Exceeding the optimized violation threshold is exactly all scenarios missing
    that fixed epsilon-mass CDF upper region, not an assumed miss probability. -/
theorem actual_optimized_interval_risk_event_iff_every_sample_misses_upper_region
    {Θ Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] (law : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (domain : Set ℝ) (C : Θ→Set ℝ) (one : Θ→ℝ) (hmeas : Measurable one)

    (X : Fin n→Ω→Θ) (epsilon : ℝ) :
    {w | epsilon<actualViolation law C (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (X i w)))}=
      {w | ∀i,X i w∉{t | 1-epsilon≤cdf (law.map one) (one t)}} := by
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (law.map one) :=
    (Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map_iff hmeas.aemeasurable).mpr inferInstance

      (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (X i w)))}=
      {w | epsilon<violation (law.map one) (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>one (X i w)))} := by
    ext w
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
    rw [actual_interval_optimized_risk_equals_the_cdf_tail law domain C one hmeas
      hconv hOne n hJoint (fun i=>X i w),
      actual_fresh_constraint_violation_is_one_minus_its_cdf]
  rw [heq,actual_optimized_violation_event_is_all_cdf_coordinates_below_threshold]
  ext w

/-- The literal one-variable scenario tail inequality has its exact logarithmic
threshold for arbitrary admissible violation and confidence parameters. -/
theorem actual_generic_one_dimensional_scenario_logarithmic_threshold

    Real.log_pow,hlog,div_le_iff₀ hden]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

def removedFeasible {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (removedIndex : ι) : Set ℝ :=
  {x | x ∈ domain ∧ ∀ j, j ≠ removedIndex → x ∈ constraints j}

def linearSupportsAt {ι : Type*} (a : ℝ) (domain : Set ℝ)
    (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ) (removedIndex : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x, x ∈ removedFeasible domain constraints removedIndex ∧ a*x < a*optimum

/-- Uniqueness belongs to the actual removed program, not to an arbitrary selected
point from a nonunique optimum set. Equal cost would make the original feasible
optimizer a second optimizer of that removed program. -/
theorem actual_changed_unique_removed_optimizer_iff_strict_objective_improvement
    {ι : Type*} (a : ℝ) (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum removedOptimum : ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hopt : optimum ∈ feasible domain constraints)
    (hremovedMin : ∀ x ∈ removedFeasible domain constraints i, a*removedOptimum ≤ a*x)
    (hremovedUnique : ∀ x ∈ removedFeasible domain constraints i,
      a*x = a*removedOptimum → x = removedOptimum) :
    removedOptimum ≠ optimum ↔ a*removedOptimum < a*optimum := by
  have hoptRemoved : optimum ∈ removedFeasible domain constraints i :=
    ⟨hopt.1, fun j _ => hopt.2 j⟩
  constructor
  · intro hchanged
    have hle := hremovedMin optimum hoptRemoved
    by_contra hnot
    have heq : a*optimum = a*removedOptimum := le_antisymm (le_of_not_gt hnot) hle
    exact hchanged (hremovedUnique optimum hoptRemoved heq).symm
  · intro hstrict hequal
    rw [hequal] at hstrict
    exact (lt_irrefl _) hstrict

theorem actual_changed_unique_removed_optimizer_iff_actual_linear_support_witness
    {ι : Type*} (a : ℝ) (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum removedOptimum : ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hopt : optimum ∈ feasible domain constraints)
    (hremovedMem : removedOptimum ∈ removedFeasible domain constraints i)
    (hremovedMin : ∀ x ∈ removedFeasible domain constraints i, a*removedOptimum ≤ a*x)
